history.en: Merriam-Webster records the first known use of the complete expression bird’s-eye view in 1771, referring to its literal high-angle meaning. This date identifies an early surviving record; it should not be treated as proof that the expression was invented in that year.
history.zh: Merriam-Webster 把 bird’s-eye view 這個完整表達的最早已知記錄追溯至1771年，當時使用的是從高處觀看的字面意思。 這個年份只代表目前找到的早期文字記錄，並不證明這個表達在該年才被創造。

history.en: The physical image naturally developed into a metaphor. Just as a flying bird can see a whole area at once, a reader, manager or learner can step back from individual details and understand the overall subject. Modern dictionaries therefore record both the physical view from above and the figurative meaning of an overall, brief look at something.
history.zh: 這個實際畫面自然發展成比喻。 正如飛鳥可以同時看見一大片地方，讀者、管理人員或學生也可以暫時離開個別細節，從整體角度了解一個主題。 因此，現代詞典同時記錄了從高處觀看的字面意思，以及概括了解整體情況的比喻意思。

origin.memoryEn: A bird sees the whole area from above; a bird’s-eye view helps you see the whole subject before studying its smaller parts.
origin.memoryZh: 飛鳥從高處看見整片地方；a bird’s-eye view 則幫助你先掌握整個主題，再研究較小的部分。

rules.titleZh: 規則一：保留完整目標表達
rules.en: Bird’s-eye may function separately as an adjective in expressions such as a bird’s-eye photograph, but that is not the complete target in this exercise.
rules.zh: bird’s-eye 可以在其他句子中作形容詞，例如 a bird’s-eye photograph，但這不是本練習所要求的完整目標表達。

rules.en: Natural English may also contain the bird’s-eye view or plural bird’s-eye views in other contexts, but they are not the locked target of this set.
rules.zh: 真實英語中也可能出現 the bird’s-eye view 或複數 bird’s-eye views，但它們並不是本練習鎖定的目標形式。
